note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official list as published by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guides are our own words, written from those descriptions and general GTA knowledge. GTA VI launched 19 November 2026, so steps that could not yet be checked in the game are marked as unverified — treat the in-game prompts and the Stats screen as the final word where a step says so.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is the reward for everything else: it unlocks automatically the moment the other 54 trophies are yours, so there is no separate task to do for it. Treat this guide's five-stage roadmap as the plan — story first (stages 1-2), strangers, activities and collectibles next (stage 3), the counted grinds after that (stage 4), and 100% completion last (stage 5). Budget roughly 60-100 hours in total; the story is the short part and the cleanup is where the hours go. Use the checklist on this page to see what is left at a glance, and tick trophies off as you earn them so the final push is never a mystery.
steps: Clear every story trophy in stages 1-2 by playing the chapters in order
Finish stranger strands, activities and collectibles in stage 3
Grind stunts, races, challenges and Shooting Range golds in stage 4
Open Stats and check the in-game 100% tracker before the final push
Earn the last remaining trophy — the platinum pops with it
tips: Read the Missables tab before you start the story — five trophies need a manual save at the right moment
Do the counted grinds after the story, when you own the full weapon set and know the map
pitfalls: Chasing the platinum trophy itself: there is nothing to do for it directly, so a checklist that only shows the platinum will never move
sources: Exophase — official GTA VI trophy list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (grade, progress targets)

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Story trophy, impossible to miss: finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission that introduces Lucia, Jason and Leonida. It plays as a guided tutorial — driving, moving on foot and the fishing beat the mission is named after — so just follow the on-screen prompts until the mission-complete screen. There is no way to fail it permanently; a failed attempt simply restarts from the last checkpoint. Use the mission to get comfortable with the driving and the fishing controls, because both come back later as full activities with their own trophies.
steps: Start a new game and play Gone Fishing
Follow the tutorial prompts as they appear
Complete the fishing beat the mission is named after
The trophy pops at the mission-complete screen
tips: Pay attention to the fishing tutorial — the same reeling and line-tension mechanics return in the fishing challenge against Cal
No preparation is needed; the mission supplies everything it asks for
pitfalls: None — this is the opening mission and cannot be missed
sources: Exophase — official GTA VI trophy list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (grade, progress targets)

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish Chapter 1 by playing its story missions in order. Side activities are optional and nothing in the chapter locks you out — a failed mission can simply be retried from the pause menu, and you keep whatever you earned up to the checkpoint. Use the chapter to learn Vice City's streets, because later chapters send you back over them, and to get a feel for which cars handle well for you. The trophy pops on the chapter-complete card, so if it has not appeared yet you still have a Chapter 1 mission left to play.
steps: Play each Chapter 1 story mission in order
Retry any failed mission from the pause menu
Learn the Vice City street layout as you drive between missions
The trophy pops on the chapter-complete card
tips: Explore between missions — early exploration feeds the Goodtime State and vehicle-discovery counters
Keep a car you like handling in mind for later; garages come later in the game
pitfalls: Skipping the chapter-complete card: the trophy only pops when the whole chapter is done, not after its longest mission
sources: Exophase — official GTA VI trophy list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (grade, progress targets)

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish Chapter 2. The chapter opens more of Leonida and brings in new contacts; keep following the story markers and the trophy follows. As you play, note where stranger '?' markers appear — they stay available after the story, which matters for the cleanup stages, and a marker you walk past now is one you will not have to hunt for later. Missions in this chapter start asking for a little more driving and a little more shooting, so buy armour when you can afford it and keep a sturdy car nearby.

Note stranger markers that appear for later cleanup
Buy armour when you can afford it before the bigger shootouts
The trophy pops on the chapter-complete card
tips: Screenshot or remember stranger marker locations — they feed the Strangers & Freaks silver
Side activities you try now count toward Master of None, so try one of each as they appear
pitfalls: None — nothing in this chapter is missable

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish Chapter 3. The story now ranges across Vice City and the wider state, missions get longer and the drives between them grow, so keep a fast car stored in a garage and fill up on ammo before the long drives. Nothing in this chapter is missable — complete it and the trophy pops — but it is a good moment to check your side progress: have you tried a few activities, picked up any collectible cards, or found a meditation spot? Anything you do now is progress you will not have to grind later.

Keep a fast, sturdy car in your garage for the long drives
Stock ammo before missions that take you far out of town
The trophy pops on the chapter-complete card

pitfalls: Running the chapter on an empty wallet: ammo and armour are cheap compared with a failed retry

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the finale. Expect the hardest shootouts of the story so far — buy armour and ammo before the big set-pieces, fight from cover, and use Combat Focus when the game offers it, because the same skill comes back as its own trophy (Gunslinger) later. If a mission keeps beating you, lower the difficulty in the settings rather than burning an evening on it; the trophy does not care what difficulty you played on. The trophy pops on the chapter-complete card.

Stock armour and ammo before set-piece missions
Fight from cover and use Combat Focus in the big firefights
The trophy pops on the chapter-complete card
tips: Practise Combat Focus here — taking down 5 enemies in one use is the Gunslinger trophy
Make a manual save before the chapter's final mission; the finale is close after this
pitfalls: Forgetting to save: the finale and the choice trophy sit just past this chapter, and a fresh save is your safety net

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Gold and unmissable: complete the final mission. Before starting it, make a manual save — the finale is the natural moment to finish any last story-linked cleanup, and the choice-flavoured trophy (Actions Speak Louder) sits close to the end of the story, so a save lets you see more than one outcome. Play the finale through to the credits; the trophy pops when the mission completes. After the credits you can keep playing in free roam, so nothing is lost by finishing the story — the whole cleanup stage happens after it.

Clear any story-linked side content first
Play the final mission through to the credits
The trophy pops at the mission-complete screen
tips: Save in a fresh slot so you can reload the finale and try the other story choice

pitfalls: Starting the finale with no manual save and then wanting to revisit the story choice — the save is the only way back

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Unmissable story-mission trophy: complete Breakfast Run. It unlocks by playing through the chapters, so just follow the story markers until it appears and finish it. No special preparation is needed; if you fail, retry it from the pause menu and you will restart at the last checkpoint with your loadout intact. The name points at trust between the two leads, and the mission is a good early look at how partner missions work — a mechanic that matters for the two partner trophies, Hot Together and Retail Therapy, which are possibly missable, so start paying attention to partner moments from here.

Play the mission through to the end

The trophy pops at the mission-complete screen

pitfalls: None — the mission is unmissable and retriable

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Unmissable story-mission trophy: complete The Cartel Heist. Heists run in stages, so expect setup beats before the main job — follow each objective marker and the trophy pops when the heist ends. Bring armour: heists tend to end in a shootout, and the escape drive is usually the hardest part. Heist income also feeds the money trophies later — Marked Bills from jobs like this are what you launder for Dime on the Dollar, and the cash funds the garage purchases for Little Boxes — so a heist is never just a story beat.

Clear its setup beats, then the main job

The name points at a family thread; beyond the usual armour and a decent car, no preparation is needed. If you fail a section, the pause menu retry puts you back at the checkpoint, so the only cost of a failure is a minute of your time.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Unmissable story-mission trophy: complete Headliners. Play the story until it unlocks and finish it. The name points at a show-business thread, so expect a set-piece around a venue or a crowd — follow the prompts as they appear and the trophy pops at the mission-complete screen. Crowd set-pieces often mix on-foot sections with a driving escape, so keep a vehicle in mind for the exit and do not get boxed in by the crowd.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Unmissable story-mission trophy: complete the VCIA Takedown at Vice City International Airport. Airport missions usually mean runways, hangars and a getaway — keep a fast vehicle ready for the escape leg and expect a wanted level on the way out. The airport is also the home of the Catch Me If You Can trophy (an unscheduled departure in a stolen plane), so learn the runway layout while you are here: the same geography serves both trophies, and a plane you spot during this mission is one you can come back for.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Unmissable story-mission trophy: complete Operation Savage Glory. The military-style name points at a heavy combat mission — stock armour, a good rifle and plenty of ammo before starting, fight from cover, and lean on Combat Focus in the big firefights. Expect waves rather than a single push: clear each wave from cover before advancing, and do not sprint into open ground between waves. If you keep dying on the same section, drop the difficulty for that mission — the trophy does not care.

Buy armour, rifle ammo and snacks first

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Gold, and the last trophy most players will earn: attain 100% completion. The in-game Stats screen shows the 100% checklist — story, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and the counted grinds (stunts, races, challenges). Work through this guide's roadmap stage by stage and check the Stats tracker regularly so you know which category is holding you back; the exact 100% requirements were not fully confirmed at launch, so treat the in-game tracker as the source of truth, not any checklist on the internet. When the tracker hits 100%, this trophy and usually the platinum pop together.

Finish story, strangers, activities and collectibles
Clear the counted grinds (stunts, races, challenges)
Re-check the tracker after each category — it names what is left
The trophy pops when the tracker hits 100%
tips: The tracker is the authority: if a category reads short, that category is your next job
Do the grinds last — story and side content fill most of the tracker on their own
pitfalls: Trusting an online 100% checklist over the in-game tracker — the tracker is what the game counts
Leaving a missable trophy behind: the five flagged trophies can block 100% if they are gone
sources: Exophase — official GTA VI trophy list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (grade, progress targets)

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts — stunt jumps, near-misses, airtime and similar driving feats, tracked across the whole game. This is a pure grind, best left until after the story when you know the map. Use a fast bike for jumps, look for stunt-jump ramps marked around Leonida, and chain near-misses on the highways: a highway run in a fast car, weaving past traffic without crashing, racks up near-misses faster than hunting individual jumps. Your count is on the Stats screen — check it before you start grinding so you know how far the story already took you.

Use a fast bike and marked stunt jumps
Chain near-misses and airtime on highways
Repeat until 250 — it stacks across all play
tips: Near-misses on a busy highway are the fastest farm: speed past traffic without touching it
Stunt jumps count once per jump, so rotate between ramps rather than repeating one
pitfalls: Crashing ends a near-miss chain — brake early and pick gaps in traffic instead of threading them at full speed

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once: fishing, the Shooting Range, drone races, arcade games, bowling, meditation, hunting, racing and the stranger activities. You do not need to be good at any of them — one attempt each counts. Work through the activity icons on the map and tick each off; most unlock early in the story. The exact list of activity types was not fully confirmed at launch, so use the in-game activity list as the authority: if a type shows as untried there, that is your next stop.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Silver: earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges, per the official list. This is a skill grind — each challenge scores accuracy, time and headshots — so expect to replay the hard ones several times. Use the recommended weapon for each challenge, shoot from cover where it is allowed, and replay a challenge until gold; your best medal is kept, so every attempt is progress. Do it after the story, when you own the full weapon set and have ammo to burn. Start with the challenges you are closest to gold on — quick wins build the habit — and save the hardest weapon types for last, when your aim is warm.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location. Drone races are time trials through rings — learn each track with a slow practice run first, then race it cleanly. Cut corners only where the rings allow it and keep the drone low and steady through the gates; altitude changes cost more time than they save. Every location needs a win, not just a finish, so a second-place run at a location does not count. The locations are spread across Leonida, so pair each race with nearby exploration for The Goodtime State and the WAiNK locations.

Practice the track once before racing it
Race cleanly through every ring — a win is required
Win at every location — a finish is not enough
tips: A slow practice run that learns the ring order beats three fast runs that miss a gate
Keep the drone low and steady; climbing and diving wastes seconds on every ring
pitfalls: Missing a ring: most races fail on one missed gate, not on raw speed
sources: Exophase — official GTA VI trophy list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (grade, progress targets)

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Races count per distinct event, so winning the same race twice does not help — you need 20 different ones across street races, off-road and whatever else the map offers. Race during the story when events appear and mop up the rest after; a fast tuned car and clean racing lines matter more than aggression, and ramming rivals usually costs you more time than it costs them. Check the race list in the game to see which events you have already won, and prioritise the ones you have not tried yet.

tips: Learn each track with one slow lap before racing it for the win

pitfalls: Re-winning a race you already won: it feels like progress and counts for nothing

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing challenges are head-to-head: catch the target fish faster, or more of them, than Cal. Use the best rod and bait you have, watch the line tension, and reel steadily — snapping the line wastes the most time. Cal is a named rival, so the challenge unlocks through the fishing thread; keep fishing until it appears, and fish in the spots the thread points you to rather than at random. If you lose, you can retry the challenge — the trophy is about the win, not the first attempt.

pitfalls: Snapping the line by reeling through a strong run — ease off when the fish fights

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete an arcade game. Find an arcade machine — in bars, arcades and some businesses around Vice City — and play one game through to its end. Any game counts; pick the shortest one you find. No score target is needed, just a completed run, so do not chase a high score when a quick finish is all the trophy asks for. If the first machine's game is long or hard, walk away and try another machine — the trophy counts any completed game on any machine.

If you are short in cleanup, buy an expensive car or weapon to close the gap. Weapons and ammo are the natural spend during the story, clothes and cars during cleanup — spread the spending across shop types, since the trophy counts all of them, and check the total in Stats if the game shows it.
steps: Buy gear, clothes and vehicles as you play
All shop spending accumulates toward $100,000
Top up with a big purchase if short at the end
The trophy pops at $100,000 spent
tips: Weapons and ammo during the story, cars and clothes during cleanup — the total builds itself
An expensive car is the fastest top-up if you are a few thousand short
pitfalls: Hoarding cash for garages while this sits unfinished — spend on gear first, garages are a separate trophy

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties. Garages are bought across Leonida and each one costs serious money — save for them, and buy them once your laundering and heist income is flowing. Check the property / real-estate screens for the full list so none is missed; the trophy pops on the last purchase. Buy garages in stage 4, after the money trophies are moving: the same laundered cash that feeds Dime on the Dollar funds these purchases, and a garage in each region also gives you somewhere to store the cars you need for races and stunts.
steps: Check the property screens for the garage list
Save heist and laundering income for garages
Buy every garage property
The trophy pops on the last purchase
tips: Buy garages after the story, when heist and laundering income is flowing
The property screen is the checklist — buy from the list, not from memory
pitfalls: Buying garages early and running out of cash for ammo and armour mid-story

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Use your phone's Scooter Bros app to register vehicles you own or find — open the app near a vehicle and register it. Ten different vehicles count; work through your garage and any interesting cars you find on the street. The quickest path is to walk down a row of parked cars and register each one in turn, then finish the set from your own garage. Registration is free and takes seconds per vehicle, so this is one of the cheapest trophies in the guide.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app on your phone
Register vehicles — 10 different ones
Use your garage cars plus street finds
The trophy pops on the tenth registration
tips: Parked rows are the fastest farm — register each car in turn
Your own garage cars count, so start there before hunting the streets
pitfalls: Registering the same vehicle twice: only different vehicles count
